title: Complementary Quantum Correlations Are Universal for Qubits
authors: Jinbo Wang, Qihang Wang, Kun Chen
abstract: Extracting total correlations from a quantum system usually requires reconstructing its state, whereas many experiments access only a few measurement settings. A possible shortcut is to add the mutual informations obtained from complementary measurements; in dimensions above two, however, this procedure can count the same classical correlation twice. We establish that qubits are protected from such overcounting. For every two-qubit state, the correlations observed in two complementary local bases are bounded by the premeasurement quantum mutual information. The proof traces this protection to binary-entropy curvature on the Bloch ball and combines a qubit information-exclusion tradeoff with data processing under local dephasing. Consequently, two correlation tables give a tomography-free lower bound on total correlation. A score above one bit also certifies a quantitative one-way entanglement-distillation rate; when applied to the Choi state of a qubit channel, the same data lower bound its quantum capacity. The theorem therefore identifies both an operational use of complementarity and the trusted two-dimensional setting in which its correlation accounting is valid.
summary: This theoretical work establishes a novel lower bound on total quantum correlation for two-qubit systems by summing classical correlations measured in complementary bases. It proves this relationship holds due to unique geometric properties of qubits (binary entropy curvature). This has direct operational consequences, providing a tomography-free way to estimate entanglement and quantify the capacity of quantum channels.
main_problem: The core problem is establishing a rigorous, state-independent lower bound for the total quantum correlation (Quantum Mutual Information) when experiments can only measure correlations from limited, complementary measurement settings.
main_result: For two qubits, the sum of classical mutual informations measured in two complementary local bases provides a universal lower bound on the total quantum correlation, $I(A:B) \ge I(X_A:X_B) + I(Z_A:Z_B)$.
method: The proof relies on analyzing the geometry of the Bloch ball using binary-entropy curvature and applying advanced information theory tools like relative-entropy data processing bounds.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses exclusively on two-qubit quantum states ($ho_{AB}$) and their correlations measured via Pauli bases (X, Z). The result is highly dependent on the dimensionality being exactly two.
key_observables: Quantum Mutual Information ($I(A:B)$), Classical Mutual Information from measurements ($I(X_A:X_B)$, $I(Z_A:Z_B)$), and the derived lower bound $S_{XZ}$.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the system (must be qubits, $d=2$), and the specific choice of complementary bases (e.g., X and Z).
main_assumptions: The result is strictly valid for two-qubit systems; in higher dimensions ($d \ge 3$), complementary measurements can lead to overcounting.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, derives the mathematical inequality using entropy curvature arguments on the Bloch ball, and then applies this bound to operational tasks like certifying entanglement or bounding quantum channel capacity.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, experimentally accessible diagnostic tool ($S_{XZ}$) that bypasses the need for full state tomography to quantify fundamental resources like entanglement and mutual information in qubit systems.
